title: Tactical Pool Chess Arena
description: A strategic arena where chess pieces from ABeautifulGame are deployed around a pool table battlefield. Animated soldiers patrol the perimeter as guards. Players must drag chess pieces onto designated pool-table pockets to score points, managing a finite energy budget that obeys conservation laws, with full undo/redo support for every move.
prompt: Create a single HTML file using Three.js r170 (importmap from cdn.jsdelivr.net) that loads three GLB assets via GLTFLoader: ABeautifulGame.glb (chess set), soldier.glb (animated soldier), and pool.glb (pool/billiards table). Scene setup: place the pool table at the origin scaled appropriately as the central battlefield. Extract 6 individual chess pieces from the ABeautifulGame model and position them on the pool table's rail edges as deployable units. Place two soldier models on opposite ends of the table using AnimationMixer to play their walk/idle animations in a looping patrol. Use a PerspectiveCamera with OrbitControls, hemisphere light plus two directional lights with soft shadows enabled on a neutral ground plane. Core mechanic: the player has an Energy Budget of 100 units displayed in a HUD overlay. Each chess piece has an energy cost (pawns=8, knights=12, bishops=14, rooks=16, queen=20, king=18). The player raycasts to click-select a chess piece (highlight it with emissive glow), then clicks one of the 6 pool table pockets (marked with glowing rings) to deploy it. Deploying animates the piece sliding to the pocket with a GSAP-style tween, deducts energy, and increments score based on piece value. Conservation law: total energy spent plus remaining energy always equals 100; display both values. Multi-input coupling: holding Shift while deploying doubles the score but triples the energy cost. Holding Ctrl activates a shield mode on the nearest soldier, pausing its animation and halving the next deployment cost. Undo/Redo: maintain a full action history stack. Press Z to undo the last deployment (piece returns to rail, energy restored, score adjusted). Press Y to redo. Support at least 10 undo levels. The game ends when energy is exhausted or all pieces are deployed. Show a results panel with final score. All UI elements (energy bar, score, undo/redo buttons, modifier indicators) should be HTML overlays styled with semi-transparent dark backgrounds and white text.
